text: {"question":"How does empirically calibrating the primordial helium fraction with the Large Binocular Telescope measurement restore the ability of the cosmic microwave background to constrain the baryon density and the effective number of relativistic species, and what evidence is presented to support this claim?","reference_answer":"By fixing the helium fraction to the LBT value, the analysis regains the sensitivity of the CMB to the free‑electron fraction during recombination, which in turn restores the precision on the baryon density and the effective neutrino number to levels comparable with those obtained when the standard BBN relation is imposed. Figure 1 in the conclusions shows that the constraints on \u03c9_b and N_eff recovered with the empirical calibration match those derived under the assumption of standard BBN, demonstrating that the loss of constraining power from a BBN‑agnostic approach is fully compensated by the LBT measurement.","passage_1_contribution":"The abstract states that the LBT measurement enables cosmological constraints that are agnostic to BBN but as precise as those enforcing standard BBN predictions.","passage_2_contribution":"The conclusions explain that empirically calibrating YHe with the LBT measurement recovers the lost constraining power on \u03c9_b and N_eff, as shown in Figure 1.","joint_reason":"The question asks for the mechanism and evidence linking the LBT measurement to restored constraints, which is detailed in the conclusions but not in the abstract.","same_quantity":true}
